properties.description:
Eight cases in `crates/reflow2-core/tests/a_dangling_reference_is_found_whatever_its_degree.rs`, all passing 2026-08-29.

THE FIXTURE HAS TO DELETE ITS OWN TARGET, and that is not a convenience — it is the only route to a dangling reference now that #366's write guard refuses one directly. It is also the honest account of how real ones arise: a target retired or renamed after the record was written.

WHAT IS PINNED:
① the regression — an ATTACHED node with a broken pointer is reported. This is the case that was silent, 2 of the 9 measured.
② the edgeless case still reported, so the fix does not trade one hole for another.
③ no double-report: the edgeless case satisfies both rules' conditions and must arrive once.
④ a resolving reference is NOT a finding, so correct work costs nothing.
⑤ a park does not silence it, asserted rather than left to be discovered because the same ruling DOES silence `orphan_node` one rule over.
⑥ the population counts references rather than nodes — four nodes with no reference property examine ZERO.
⑦ the message names both the property and the unresolvable id.
⑧ no repair is proposed and the finding says why.

⚠️ THE PRE-STATE IS ASSERTED, NOT DESCRIBED, and this is the part worth keeping. These tests cannot be run against the old build — `HealCategory::DanglingReference` did not exist, so they would not compile — and a test that only ever passes is no evidence about the bug it names. Case ① therefore also asserts that `orphan_node` does NOT report the attached node, which is the condition that made the rule necessary and is checkable on both sides of the change. If that assertion ever fails, the two rules have started to overlap and the de-duplication needs rethinking.

Two class guards elsewhere were forced to answer for the new category rather than being updated silently: `every_category_is_listed_in_all` (heal.rs) and `every_category_states_whether_it_reads_proposed` (tests/proposed_asserts_nothing.rs). Both are exhaustive matches with no wildcard, which is why the compiler stopped the build until each was answered.
properties.findings:
8 passed, 0 failed, on the full `cargo test -p reflow2-core` run (201 lib + every integration suite green).

TWO THINGS THE RUN ESTABLISHED THAT THE PASS COUNT DOES NOT SHOW:

① THE COMPILER, NOT A REVIEWER, FOUND THE THREE PLACES A NEW CATEGORY HAD TO ANSWER. Adding the variant broke the build in `heal.rs` (propose_heal's repair dispatch), `ility.rs` (`axes_for`), and `tests/proposed_asserts_nothing.rs` (the reads-proposed class guard) — every one an exhaustive match written with no wildcard precisely so this would happen. `every_category_is_listed_in_all` then failed on its hand-maintained count until `ALL` was extended, which is the check its own comment says exists because "a category missing from ALL would make that claim quietly short".

② THE FIXTURES CANNOT WRITE A DANGLING REFERENCE DIRECTLY, so each creates its target and deletes it. That is #366's write guard working, observed from the test side rather than asserted — and it is why the read-side rule was needed at all: the only remaining routes to a broken pointer are a retire, a rename, or a value written before that guard existed.
properties.name: A dangling node reference is reported whatever the node's degree, status or ruling
